verses.text: Now Balaam saw that the LORD was pleased to bless Israel, so he did not go to look for signs as he had done before. Instead, he turned and looked toward the desert.
When Balaam looked up, he saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came on him.
Then he spoke his message: "This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
the message of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the All-Powerful, who bows down with his eyes wide open:
How beautiful are your tents, people of Jacob, your homes, people of Israel!
They spread out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloe plants planted by the LORD, like cedar trees beside the water.
Water will flow from their buckets, and their seed will have plenty of water. Their king will be greater than Agag, and their kingdom will be lifted high.
God brought them out of Egypt. He is like the strength of a wild ox for them. They will eat up the nations that are their enemies. They will break their bones in pieces and strike them with arrows.
Like a lion they lie down to rest, like a lioness. Who would dare to wake them? May everyone who blesses you be blessed, and may everyone who curses you be cursed!"
Balak became very angry with Balaam. He clapped his hands in anger and said to him, "I called you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them these three times!
Now get out of here and go home! I said I would reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from your reward."
Balaam answered Balak, "Didn't I tell the messengers you sent me,
'Even if Balak gave me his palace full of silver and gold, I could not go against the LORD's command to do anything good or bad on my own. I must say only what the LORD says'?
Now I am going back to my people. But come, let me warn you what these people will do to your people in the days to come."
Then he spoke his message: "This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
the message of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the All-Powerful, who bows down with his eyes wide open:

I see him, but not now. I look at him, but he is not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A king's royal stick will rise out of Israel. He will crush the heads of Moab, and the skulls of all the people of Sheth.
Edom will be conquered. Seir, his enemy, will be conquered, while Israel grows strong.
A ruler will come out of Jacob, and he will destroy the survivors of the city."
Then Balaam looked at Amalek and spoke this message: "Amalek was first among the nations, but in the end it will be destroyed forever."
Then he looked at the Kenites and spoke this message: "Your home is safe, like a nest set high in the rocks.
Yet you Kenites will be burned up, when Assyria takes you away as prisoners."
Then he spoke this message: "Oh, who can live when God does this?
Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus. They will crush Assyria and Eber, but they too will be destroyed forever."
Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak went on his way.
